notes: Mixed in practice: private and off-street council car parks 20%, on-street council parking and the Dart Charge and the congestion charge outside scope. Default 20% because airport car parks dominate this client's history.

notes: Public charge points 20%. Home charging is a 5% domestic supply with input tax restricted, so a home-charged receipt needs the rate overridden.

name: Staff costs
notes: ADDED. Name from Desktop's default chart. Wages are not a supply.

name: Advertising and marketing
notes: ADDED. Name from Desktop's default chart. Business entertainment shares this HMRC box and its input tax is blocked, so entertainment must not inherit this rate. See the blocked-input-tax note.

name: Computer Software
notes: Overseas suppliers may be reverse charge; override where the invoice shows no UK VAT. Desktop's equivalent is named 'Software and subscriptions'.

name: Water, Tissues & Newspapers for Passengers
notes: PHV-specific. Genuinely spans two rates: bottled water and tissues 20%, printed newspapers zero-rated. Default 20%.

name: Motor Expenses - Maintenance
notes: Desktop's 'Repairs and maintenance' is premises work; vehicle maintenance stays here.

name: Motor Expenses - Insurance
notes: Insurance is exempt. Insurance premium tax is not VAT and is not recoverable.

name: Motor Expenses
notes: Parent of 281, 282, 286, 287 and 386. Nothing should post here. Not set rather than a rate, because a parent carrying a default rate invites posting to it.

name: Subsistence
notes: Spans two rates: restaurant and hot takeaway 20%, cold takeaway food zero-rated. Default 20%.

name: Motor Expense - Car Tax
notes: VED is outside the scope. NAMING carried forward from the original draft: singular 'Expense' here, plural everywhere else.

name: Car Wash
notes: Coin-operated washes are often run by unregistered operators, so there is frequently no VAT to recover even though the rate is 20%.

name: Legal and professional fees
notes: ADDED. 292 is accountancy only. Desktop's single 'Professional fees' covers both.

name: Repairs and maintenance
notes: ADDED. Name from Desktop's default chart. Premises work; vehicle maintenance stays at 281.

name: Insurance
notes: ADDED. Name from Desktop's default chart. Non-motor only; motor insurance stays at 282. Note Desktop puts insurance in the premises box and this chart puts motor insurance in travel, so the same word reaches two HMRC boxes.

name: Postage
notes: Royal Mail's universal service, meaning ordinary stamps, is exempt. Couriers, Parcelforce and business account mail are 20%. This default is a judgement and it is the one of mine I am least sure of.

name: Interest Payable
notes: Desktop merges interest and bank charges into one category; this chart splits them across 362 and 363.

name: Use Of Home
notes: Not a purchase. A computed apportionment posted by journal, so there is no supply and no input tax.

name: Statutory Fees, Licenses and permits
notes: PHV licensing and DVLA fees are statutory functions, outside the scope.

name: Irrecoverable debts written off
notes: ADDED. The HMRC box exists in Desktop's list with no account against it.

name: Motor Expenses - Car Tax - Private Use
notes: CHECK carried forward: private-use adjustment, disallowable, and no HMRC box assigned. FLAG: the vendor mappings CSV spells this name with em dashes and this file uses hyphens, so one code has two name strings.

name: Sundry expenses
notes: ADDED. Name from Desktop's default chart. Deliberately no default rate: a catch-all that carries one is how a wrong rate gets applied confidently. A cluster of transactions here is a missing account, per section 13.

name: Equipment
notes: ADDED. Name from Desktop's default chart. The asset alternative to 271. The rate is set because input tax is recoverable on the purchase even though the account is balance sheet. FLAG: I inferred the 600s as FreeAgent's capital asset range from a sub-account example in its API docs, not from a published range table. Moderate confidence, needs checking.

name: Motor vehicles
notes: ADDED. A PHV driver's car. The supply is standard rated but input tax on a car is blocked unless it is used exclusively for business, which a PHV car normally is not. See the blocked-input-tax note: this chart cannot express that, and the rate alone will mislead.
